name: Session Guard Concurrency Coordinator
purpose: Coordinates any number of parallel project sessions (git worktrees) on one 8 GB Apple Silicon host: authoring runs in parallel, while every heavy job (Chromium render and frame-review, Kokoro TTS, reference analysis) shares one host lock and queues first-come-first-served, without compromising rendering quality.
capabilities: Single host lock: render, tts and analysis share one flock so a Kokoro job and a render never overlap; re-entrant for child processes
First-come-first-served wait queue with queue positions, dead-waiter pruning and a configurable timeout (MOTION_LAB_LOCK_TIMEOUT)
Crash safety: SIGTERM/SIGHUP/SIGINT on a holder kills its whole job tree (including detached Chrome helpers) before the lock is released; a dead holder frees the flock automatically
status: lock holder, ordered queue and free-memory advisory; unlock [--force] clears stale state or stops a hung holder

Git worktree sessions without a session cap: session-start (warns about uncommitted tooling), session-list (ahead/behind, uncommitted, unmerged renders, predicted merge conflicts, shared files touched, lock activity), session-end (conflict pre-check, copies gitignored renders/audio/out back to main, non-interactive merge)
Self-guarding entry points via src/pipeline/hostlock.py: build-audio, tts, frame-review, reference-corpus and the shell render stages lock without a wrapper

installation.instructions: Built-in workspace tool. Run via python3 scripts/session-guard.py <subcommand>.

compatibility.notes: Uses standard library fcntl.flock on POSIX macOS; reads vm_stat and ps for the memory advisory and process-tree teardown.

security.notes: Writes lockfiles and queue tickets to .locks/, signals only its own descendant processes, and runs git worktree/merge commands in this repository.

approval_evidence: Cross-process tests in tests/test-studio.py (SessionGuardTests): shared tts/render lock, FIFO order, dead-waiter pruning, SIGTERM teardown of a detached grandchild, worktree rescue/conflict/merge lifecycle, re-entrancy. Run on the macOS host on 2026-11-05.
